propositions: The ADR-promised byte-total backstop trigger was never implemented in _gc_pass, which only consults free disk space and mtime but never reads _cache.byte_total, leaving no size-cap-based reclamation mechanism.

materialize_tickets populates store entries by directly renaming files without calling add_bytes, causing tickets entries (~620 MiB each, the store's dominant entries) to be completely absent from the byte-total accounting.

The combination of the missing backstop and unaccounted entries allowed the snapshot store to grow unchecked, contributing to disk pressure breaching 85-90% on the review-bot host with no reclaim trigger firing.

A new max_bytes tunable with configurable cap and LRU eviction loop was implemented to provide the promised byte-total-driven reclamation trigger, defaulting to off to avoid changing existing deployments.
materialize_tickets now calls add_bytes on won-race branches to ensure all store entries are accounted in the incremental byte total, making it agree with startup_sweep's reconciling walk.
Five new tests validate the byte-cap trigger fires correctly, materialize_tickets accounting is exact, and the feature is default-off with no behavioral change to existing deployments.
